A mother brings her 7-year-old son to the pediatrician due to a rash that appeared suddenly the
previous day. The child recovered from an upper respiratory infection two weeks ago without requiring
treatment but is otherwise healthy with an unremarkable medical history. His vital signs show:
temperature 97.2°F (36.8°C), blood pressure 123/80 mmHg, pulse 71/min, and respirations 20/min.
The physical examination reveals a well-appearing child with a diffuse petechial rash. Laboratory
results show: Hemoglobin: 12.6 g/dL Hematocrit: 37% Leukocyte count: 5,100/mm^3 Platelet count:
65,000/mm^3 What is the most appropriate management strategy? Answer Choices: (A)
Anticoagulation therapy (B) Corticosteroid therapy (C) Platelet transfusion (D) Observation (E) Plasma
exchange (F) Hospital admission and monitoring (G) Bone marrow biopsy (H) Intravenous
immunoglobulin (IVIg) (I) Splenectomy (J) Rituximab
 A. Rituximab
B. Corticosteroid therapy
C. Hospital admission and monitoring
D. Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg)
E. Splenectomy
F. Plasma exchange
G. Bone marrow biopsy
H. Observation
I. Anticoagulation therapy
J. Platelet transfusion
